Residual hole in the (now `Self::`-aware) drift guard, invisible to ALL THREE assertions at once. `ValidationError`'s fields are `pub` (line 430-441) and the scanner only reads CONSTRUCTION sites, so `let mut e = ValidationError::err("semantic", "WORKFLOW_CYCLE", m); e.code = "WORKFLOW_NEW";` registers the already-known WORKFLOW_CYCLE and never surfaces WORKFLOW_NEW: the emitted set is unchanged, so `unregistered`/`stale` both pass, `HUMAN_COPY` is never asked for an entry, and `humaniseFinding` (validationCopy.ts:196-198) falls back to the raw wire message in front of the author — the exact silent-agreement failure mode the `Self::` fix was written to close. Every OTHER dialect is loud (`use … as`, `type X =`, struct literal, `Self { code: "…" }`, non-literal code arg). Closing it needs either private fields + accessors or a scan for `\.code\s*=` on a `ValidationError` binding.
